Question #099
My notes & example from experience
100Web Platform/SeniorHandle fetch failures, retries, and cancellation
The interview scenario

An API returns 500, but the catch block never runs. A retry sometimes creates duplicate orders.

How to answer

fetch normally resolves for HTTP error responses; check response.ok or the status before treating a body as success. Network failures and aborts are different from application validation errors. Parse only an expected body format and validate data at the boundary.

Retry only failures and operations for which retry is safe, with a bounded policy and backoff where appropriate. Mutations may need server-supported idempotency keys; a client timeout does not prove the server did nothing. Distinguish cancellation from a user-visible error and prevent stale results from replacing newer ones.

const response = await fetch("/api/products", { signal });
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
const payload = await response.json();
// Validate payload shape before it enters application state.

Common mistake

Retrying every POST automatically or assuming response.json validates the data shape.

Prove your answer

Test HTTP 500, 429, invalid JSON, timeout after server commit, and user cancellation.

Question #100
My notes & example from experience
101CSS/MidPredict the rendered width with box-sizing
The interview scenario

A panel has width: 240px, padding: 20px, and border: 4px. Why does it exceed its 240px slot?

How to answer

With content-box, the declared width describes the content box. Horizontal padding and borders add 48 pixels, giving a 288px border box. With border-box, that same 240px includes padding and borders, leaving a 192px content box. Margins sit outside both calculations.

A consistent border-box reset often makes component sizing easier, but it does not prevent overflow from intrinsically wide children. Inspect computed styles and the actual box model instead of adding arbitrary negative margins. The live lab in this guide lets you change padding and compare both calculations.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
.panel { width: 240px; padding: 20px; border: 4px solid; }

Common mistake

Including margins in the border-box width or assuming width always equals visible outer width.

Prove your answer

Check getBoundingClientRect().width and DevTools box-model measurements.

Question #101
My notes & example from experience
102CSS/SeniorFix the flex item that refuses to shrink
The interview scenario

A row contains an avatar and a long filename. The filename pushes the card outside the screen.

How to answer

A flex item can have an automatic minimum size based on its content, so flex: 1 alone may not let it shrink enough. Apply min-width: 0, or the logical min-inline-size: 0, to the item that must be allowed to shrink. Then choose wrapping, clipping, or ellipsis for the actual content.

Trace nested flex and grid items: more than one ancestor may preserve a minimum. Do not hide overflow on the entire page to conceal the symptom; that can clip focus rings and real content. The layout contract and text-overflow policy are separate decisions.

.row { display: flex; gap: 1rem; }
.text { flex: 1; min-inline-size: 0; }
.title { overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; }

Question #102
My notes & example from experience
103CSS/SeniorStop a 1fr grid column from overflowing
The interview scenario

A dashboard uses 240px 1fr, but a large preformatted code block pushes the main column beyond the viewport.

How to answer

A flexible grid track can retain an automatic minimum that is influenced by min-content sizing. minmax(0, 1fr) explicitly lets the flexible track shrink below that content minimum. Also constrain the grid child and give the code block its own overflow policy.

The fix is not to make the text unreadably small. Keep overflow local to the content that requires it, such as a horizontal code scroller. When designing reusable grids, test unusually long content and not only short placeholder labels.

.shell { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 240px minmax(0, 1fr); }
main { min-inline-size: 0; }

Question #103
My notes & example from experience
104CSS/MidChoose Grid or Flexbox for a component
The interview scenario

A team uses nested flex rows for a pricing comparison and struggles to align columns across rows.

How to answer

Flexbox is well suited to distributing and aligning items primarily along one dimension. Grid defines relationships across rows and columns and is often easier when track alignment is part of the design. The two work well together; this is not a framework-wide either-or choice.

Start with content and relationships: a wrapping toolbar may be flex, while aligned pricing cells may need grid or a semantic table depending on meaning. Preserve appropriate HTML semantics. Visual similarity alone does not make a data table equivalent to a collection of divs.

Question #104
My notes & example from experience
105CSS/MidDebug position: sticky that never sticks
The interview scenario

A sidebar has position: sticky, but it either scrolls away or stops immediately.

How to answer

A sticky element needs a non-auto inset on the axis of sticking, such as top: 1rem. Its behavior depends on the nearest ancestor with a scrolling mechanism and is constrained by its containing block. Unexpected overflow on an ancestor can therefore change which scroll container matters.

The element also needs room to travel; a sidebar as tall as its container or stretched to the full grid row can appear not to stick. Inspect ancestor overflow, heights, alignment, and containment before replacing sticky with JavaScript scroll positioning.

.sidebar { position: sticky; inset-block-start: 1rem; align-self: start; }

Prove your answer

Question #105
My notes & example from experience
106CSS/SeniorExplain why z-index: 999999 loses
The interview scenario

A tooltip with a huge z-index remains underneath a neighboring panel.

How to answer

z-index is interpreted within stacking contexts rather than one global page-wide number line. Ancestors with properties such as transforms, opacity below one, isolation, or certain positioned z-index values can create a stacking context. A descendant cannot escape its ancestor context merely by using a larger number.

Inspect the ancestor chain and decide whether to change the stacking architecture, remove an unnecessary context, or render an overlay elsewhere through a portal. Browser top-layer elements, such as modal dialogs, have distinct placement behavior. Use a small documented layer scale instead of an arms race of arbitrary values.

Common mistake

Increasing the child z-index without inspecting the ancestor that controls its entire context.

Prove your answer

Find the nearest stacking-context creators and inspect the overlay under transformed parents.

The interviewer goes deeperHow does rendering into document.body change the problem, and what problems remain?

Question #106
My notes & example from experience
107CSS/SeniorResolve overrides with cascade layers
The interview scenario

A component library and application CSS keep fighting, producing increasingly specific selectors.

How to answer

The cascade considers origin, importance, and layer precedence before specificity among otherwise competing rules. For normal author declarations, later layers beat earlier layers, while unlayered normal styles outrank layered normal styles. Important declarations reverse layer ordering, so !important is not a harmless shortcut.

Define a deliberate layer contract for resets, vendor styles, tokens, components, and utilities. Use DevTools to see why the winning declaration wins. Source order is only decisive after higher-priority cascade criteria tie; a longer selector is not a universal override strategy.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
@layer reset, vendor, components, utilities;
@layer components { .button { border-radius: .5rem; } }
@layer utilities { .rounded-none { border-radius: 0; } }
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Saying the last class in HTML wins or applying important without understanding layer reversal.

Prove your answer

Inspect crossed-out declarations and test overrides with and without an unlayered vendor rule.

The interviewer goes deeperWhy can a low-specificity unlayered rule beat a more-specific layered rule?
DocumentationMDN: CSS cascade ↗
Question #107
My notes & example from experience
108CSS/SeniorUse :where(), :is(), and :has() without specificity surprises
The interview scenario

A design-system selector becomes hard to override after a selector list includes an ID.

How to answer

:where() contributes zero specificity, including its arguments, which is useful for low-priority defaults. :is() and :has() take specificity from the most specific relevant selector in their argument list; an ID can therefore raise the rule's weight unexpectedly. :has() also lets a subject match based on a relative selector.

Use these features to express relationships clearly, not to build opaque selectors spanning the entire application. Keep a component boundary and test matching as well as precedence. Complex stateful UI still needs correct HTML semantics and sometimes JavaScript.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
:where(.theme) .button { font: inherit; }
.field:has(input:invalid) { border-color: crimson; }
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Assuming every modern functional pseudo-class has zero specificity.

Prove your answer

Calculate selector weights, then inspect the actual matched rule in DevTools.

Question #108
My notes & example from experience
109CSS/SeniorMake a card respond to its container, not the viewport
The interview scenario

The same card appears in a narrow sidebar and a wide content area on the same desktop viewport.

How to answer

A viewport media query cannot distinguish those two available widths. Establish a query container on an ancestor using container-type: inline-size, then change descendant layout with an @container size query. Named containers help when several containment levels exist.

The queried element needs a suitable ancestor container; do not expect an element to query its own width and freely resize itself without containment rules. Choose a stable baseline layout, and use container queries for component adaptation rather than making every small styling decision depend on JavaScript measurements.

.card { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }

Question #109
My notes & example from experience
110CSS/SeniorAlign nested cards using subgrid
The interview scenario

Product cards have different title lengths. Their prices and buttons no longer align across the row.

How to answer

Subgrid lets a nested grid use the tracks of its parent along a chosen axis. That allows content inside separate cards to align to shared rows without imposing brittle fixed heights. The card must span the relevant parent tracks and opt into subgrid for the intended dimension.

Use a meaningful fallback for supported-browser requirements and preserve natural content flow. Subgrid is a track-sharing mechanism, not automatic equalization of unrelated DOM structures. Verify how gaps, spanning, and dynamic content interact with the parent grid.

.products { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 1rem; }

Question #110

111CSS/MidBuild fluid typography without breaking zoom
The interview scenario

A heading scales smoothly on desktop but becomes too small on phones and poorly responds to user text settings.

How to answer

clamp(minimum, preferred, maximum) provides bounds for a fluid value. Combining relative font units with a viewport term can be more resilient than viewport-only sizing, but the entire design still needs zoom and reflow testing. A maximum can cap growth, so do not assume a clamp expression is automatically accessible.

Avoid fixed heights around fluid text and choose readable line lengths. For viewport-height layouts, distinguish available viewport behavior and dynamic browser UI rather than blindly applying 100vh. Let content grow when translations or accessibility settings require more room.

Question #111

112CSS/MidSupport right-to-left layouts with logical properties
The interview scenario

An English dashboard is being localized to Arabic, and dozens of left/right overrides are appearing.

How to answer

Logical properties express relationships in inline and block directions rather than physical left and right. margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end, inline-size, and text-align: start can adapt to writing direction and writing mode. This reduces duplicated direction-specific rules.

Not every visual object should mirror: a media timeline or a geographically meaningful image may retain its direction. Set meaningful document direction and test mixed-direction strings, numbers, and icons. Logical CSS helps layout, but does not solve translation or bidirectional text handling by itself.

How to answer

An ellipsis needs an overflow situation and a compatible layout: for a single line, constrain the available width, prevent wrapping, and clip overflowing text. In a flex or grid layout, the containing item may also need its automatic minimum removed. text-overflow alone does not create those conditions.

Treat truncation as a content decision. Essential values may need wrapping, expansion, or another discoverable presentation rather than being hidden. A title attribute is not a complete keyboard- and touch-friendly solution to recovering clipped information.

Question #113
My notes & example from experience
114CSS/SeniorChoose animation properties with rendering costs in mind
The interview scenario

Animating left on 100 cards makes scrolling stutter, and someone proposes will-change on every element.

How to answer

Changing layout-affecting properties can trigger layout and paint work. Transform and opacity are often better candidates for compositor-friendly animation, but actual performance depends on layer promotion, content, and browser behavior. Measure instead of treating any property as a guarantee of free GPU work.

Use will-change sparingly and remove it when no longer needed; excessive layers can increase memory and compositing costs. Keep movement purposeful and account for reduced-motion preferences. A visual effect that performs well on a powerful laptop can still be costly on a low-memory phone.

.card { transition: transform 160ms ease; }
.card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); }

Question #114

115CSS/MidRespect reduced motion without removing meaning
The interview scenario

A route transition zooms the whole screen. Some users request reduced motion.

How to answer

Use prefers-reduced-motion to reduce or replace nonessential movement. A subtle immediate state change can preserve feedback without large spatial animation. Do not remove essential progress information; change its presentation so the user still understands what happened.

Apply the preference to CSS, JavaScript animations, smooth scrolling, and framework transitions. Prefer a baseline that remains usable without motion. Test the reduced-motion path as an intentional design, not as a universal duration hack that accidentally breaks event-dependent logic.

Question #115

116CSS/SeniorUse content-visibility without confusing it with virtualization
The interview scenario

A long article is expensive to render, but removing offscreen sections would break search and reading flow.

How to answer

content-visibility: auto can let the browser skip rendering work for offscreen content while retaining it in the DOM. An intrinsic size estimate can reduce jumps before the content is measured. This is different from virtualization, which typically removes or recycles DOM nodes.

It does not eliminate the cost of creating all data and JavaScript objects, nor every memory cost. Check accessibility behavior and avoid forcing layout on skipped subtrees through measurement code. Use it where the content can safely be contained and test the effect on scroll stability.

  contain-intrinsic-size: auto 600px; }

Question #116

117CSS/SeniorDesign readable light and dark themes

Use semantic color tokens for text, surfaces, borders, status, and focus rather than inverting a palette mechanically. Under WCAG contrast requirements, normal text generally needs 4.5:1 and qualifying large text 3:1, with defined exceptions. Evaluate the actual foreground/background combination.

Test state combinations and real font sizes, not just palette swatches. Distinguish disabled controls from low-emphasis interactive controls, and do not convey errors only through color. Dark mode should preserve hierarchy and focus visibility rather than merely changing the page background.

Flex and Grid visual reordering can leave DOM, reading, and sequential keyboard order unchanged. Write source order to express the logical reading and interaction sequence, then use layout to arrange it without making the two sequences conflict.

Avoid patching the problem with positive tabindex values; they create a separate fragile navigation order. When a responsive design genuinely needs a different information structure, review the design and semantics instead of duplicating interactive content carelessly. Question #124
My notes & example from experience
125Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind v4+Resolve conflicting utilities without relying on class order
The interview scenario

A button receives `p-2 p-6`, and moving p-2 to the end of className does not change its padding.

How to answer

CSS cascade and generated stylesheet order determine which competing utility wins, not the order of tokens in an HTML class attribute. Prefer a component API that selects one intended value for a conflicting property. Conditional class assembly does not automatically understand CSS conflicts.

A conflict-aware merging library can be useful when accepting overrides, but its version and configuration must match the Tailwind vocabulary. Define which overrides the component supports; unrestricted className overrides can undermine layout and accessibility guarantees. Inspect computed styles when behavior is surprising.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
const padding = size === "compact" ? "p-2" : "p-6";
<div className={`rounded-lg ${padding}`}>...</div>
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Assuming string concatenation guarantees the last utility token wins.

Prove your answer

Inspect generated rule order and test component overrides across variants and breakpoints.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you prevent a consumer from removing a critical focus indication?
DocumentationTailwind: Utility-first styling ↗MDN: CSS cascade ↗
Question #125
My notes & example from experience
126Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind v4+Prevent a dark-mode flash and hydration mismatch
The interview scenario

The server renders a light theme, but the browser immediately reads dark mode from storage and disagrees.

How to answer

Choose a clear preference model: system, light, or dark. Tailwind can use its media-based dark variant or a custom selector-based variant for explicit user control. Apply the resolved theme early enough to reduce a flash while preserving consistent server and initial client markup.

Coordinate the theme source with SSR, caching, and CSP. A tiny early script, a server-readable preference, or a framework-aware theme solution has different trade-offs. Handle unavailable storage and system preference changes. Do not hide arbitrary hydration mismatches instead of resolving their cause.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
@import "tailwindcss";
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
/* Apply the .dark class using a deliberate SSR-compatible policy. */
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Reading localStorage during a server render or suppressing every hydration warning globally.

Prove your answer

Test first visit, saved preference, disabled storage, system theme changes, and a slow connection.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would cookie-based theme selection affect shared HTML caching?
DocumentationTailwind: Dark mode ↗React: hydrateRoot ↗
Question #126
My notes & example from experience
127Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind v4+Extract reusable components without recreating a CSS framework
The interview scenario

A codebase has long utility strings, and the team proposes replacing all of them with @apply classes.

How to answer

Extract repeated behavior and structure into components with a small variant API. A button component can own semantics, loading behavior, focus style, and a finite size/tone mapping. Repetition within a small readable template is not always a reason for another abstraction.

Use shared tokens and stable variants to keep designs coherent. @apply can help specific integration cases, but replacing every utility combination with a named class often creates a second styling system with its own indirection. Evaluate change frequency and ownership rather than line length alone.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
const sizes = { sm: "px-3 py-1.5 text-sm", md: "px-4 py-2" };
const tones = { primary: "bg-blue-600 text-white", neutral: "bg-slate-100 text-slate-900" };
// A typed component selects valid entries and owns native button semantics.
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Creating a universal component with dozens of boolean props that permit contradictory states.

Prove your answer

Change a design token and one behavior; count the places that require independent edits.

Question #127
My notes & example from experience
128Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind v4+Use @reference when isolated styles need theme context
The interview scenario

A CSS module uses @apply with a custom utility, but Tailwind cannot resolve the utility even though the main stylesheet defines it.

How to answer

In separately processed stylesheets, use @reference to make the relevant theme definitions, utilities, and variants available without emitting a duplicate copy of that stylesheet. Reference the actual shared stylesheet when it contains custom definitions; referencing Tailwind alone does not include application-specific additions.

Keep module processing and build integration consistent. Do not use @import where it would unintentionally duplicate large output. Direct CSS custom properties may be simpler than @apply for some styles, especially when the module only needs a token value.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
/* Example CSS module processed by Tailwind v4 */
@reference "../app.css";
.title { @apply font-bold text-brand-600; }

Common mistake

Importing the entire global stylesheet repeatedly to fix a missing context error.

Prove your answer

Inspect the production CSS for duplicates and verify custom token changes reach the module.

Question #128
My notes & example from experience
129Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind v4+Debug source scanning in a monorepo
The interview scenario

Utilities used by a shared UI package are absent from one application's production build.

How to answer

Confirm which directories Tailwind scans and whether the shared package is ignored or outside the detected source roots. Explicit @source declarations can include required files; source controls also help prevent scanning irrelevant large trees. Use full class tokens in the shared package.

Debug from the consuming app's real build location and clean output. Do not depend on a class being accidentally generated by another page. Keep a representative package fixture or visual test that exercises every public variant. The production artifact, not the development cache, is the evidence.

@import "tailwindcss";
@source "../../packages/ui/src";

Adding huge blanket safelists rather than fixing an incorrect source boundary.

Question #129
My notes & example from experience
130Tailwind CSS/Senior/Tailwind 4.3; 8 May 2026Evaluate a new v4.3 utility before adopting it
The interview scenario

A design request can use new scrollbar and logical-layout utilities, but the project supports several browser engines.

How to answer

Tailwind CSS 4.3 adds utilities including scrollbar styling and additional logical-direction conveniences. Treat a new utility as generated CSS with a browser-support and accessibility story, not as a cross-browser guarantee simply because the compiler accepts it.

Read the underlying property behavior, use progressive enhancement where suitable, and test the design with unsupported or overridden styling. Avoid hiding scrollbars merely for aesthetics when it makes overflow undiscoverable. Pin and verify the actual installed Tailwind release rather than copying new syntax into an older project.

Common mistake

Assuming a utility name guarantees identical rendering on every platform.

Prove your answer

Test multiple engines, keyboard scrolling, forced colors, and the fallback appearance.

Question #130
My notes & example from experience
131Testing & Quality/SeniorTest observable behavior instead of component internals
The interview scenario

A harmless refactor changes a component's state shape and CSS class names, breaking most tests.

How to answer

Write tests around what a user can perceive and do: find controls by role and accessible name, interact, and assert meaningful outcomes. getBy queries suit immediately present content, findBy awaits appearance, and queryBy is useful for absence. Scope queries when multiple similar controls exist.

Keep pure business logic tests separate when they provide clearer coverage. Avoid asserting private hook state or arbitrary class names unless that detail is the actual contract. A behavior-focused test should survive a refactor that preserves user-visible behavior, while still failing for a real regression.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
const user = userEvent.setup();
render(<Login />);
await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), "a@example.test");
await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: /sign in/i }));
expect(await screen.findByText(/welcome/i)).toBeVisible();
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Treating test IDs as a substitute for missing accessible names everywhere.

Prove your answer

Refactor component internals and confirm the test remains stable; remove the user outcome and confirm it fails.

The interviewer goes deeperWhen is a test ID a reasonable choice instead of a role query?

Question #131
My notes & example from experience
132Testing & Quality/SeniorTest a debounce without real sleeps
The interview scenario

A debounce test waits one second on every run and occasionally times out in CI.

How to answer

Use the test runner's fake clock to control timer progression and assert behavior just before and after the threshold. Test resetting the timer, cancellation, and the final arguments, not merely that a callback eventually ran. Coordinate user-event with its advanceTimers option when fake timers are enabled.

Flush appropriate pending work and restore real timers during cleanup so one test does not poison others. Promises and React updates may require their own awaited handling; advancing time is not a universal way to flush all asynchronous work.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
// Jest example; debounce is the implementation under test.
jest.useFakeTimers();
const fn = jest.fn();
const delayed = debounce(fn, 300);
delayed("a"); delayed("ab");
jest.advanceTimersByTime(299);
expect(fn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
jest.advanceTimersByTime(1);
expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledWith("ab");
jest.runOnlyPendingTimers();
jest.useRealTimers();
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Using a large real sleep or assuming fake timers automatically resolve every Promise chain.

Prove your answer

Assert no call at delay minus one, one call at delay, and none after cancellation.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you test a leading-edge debounce with a trailing invocation?
DocumentationTesting Library: Fake timers ↗
Question #132
My notes & example from experience
133Testing & Quality/SeniorRemove flaky browser waits
The interview scenario

A Playwright test uses waitForTimeout(3000) after clicking Save and still fails intermittently.

How to answer

Use locators and web-first assertions that wait for the expected observable state. Playwright's actionability checks help actions occur when an element is usable, but they do not know whether your business operation has completed. Assert the resulting confirmation or data state.

Isolate tests and seed deterministic data. Investigate traces, network activity, and console output before increasing timeouts. Retries can expose and temporarily tolerate flakiness, but a green retry is not evidence that the underlying race disappeared.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }).click();
await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText("Saved");
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Waiting for networkidle on a page with continuous polling or using arbitrary long sleeps.

Prove your answer

Run repeatedly under slower CI conditions and inspect first-failure traces.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you distinguish a real application race from a test synchronization mistake?

Question #133
My notes & example from experience
134Testing & Quality/SeniorMock the network without making tests meaningless
The interview scenario

Tests mock every internal data hook and pass even when the UI sends the wrong request payload.

How to answer

Mock at a boundary that preserves the behavior you want to test. Network interception can let the real component and request-building code run while controlling response timing, status, and content. Assert request details when they are part of the contract.

Use fixtures that reflect actual schemas and cover empty, partial, malformed, slow, and failed responses. Keep a smaller set of real integration checks to detect drift between mocks and the service. Service workers or test routing order can affect interception, so verify the mock actually handled the request.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
await page.route("**/api/products", route =>
  route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "application/json",
    body: JSON.stringify({ items: [] }) })
);
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Mocking the function under test or never validating that the fixture matches the real API.

Prove your answer

Make the request payload invalid and ensure a relevant test fails.

Question #134
My notes & example from experience
135Testing & Quality/SeniorCombine automated and manual accessibility testing
The interview scenario

An automated accessibility scan reports zero violations, but keyboard users cannot complete checkout.

How to answer

Automated rules can find many issues such as missing names or some contrast and structural problems, but they cannot prove the entire experience is accessible. Combine scans with keyboard task completion, focus-order review, screen-reader checks, zoom, and testing of error and loading states.

Scan meaningful UI states, including open dialogs and validation errors, rather than only the home page at rest. Track exceptions with justification and ownership. Accessibility is part of component behavior and acceptance criteria, not a final score that replaces user-centered testing.

Common mistake

Calling a product accessible solely because axe returned an empty violations array.

Prove your answer

Complete purchase using keyboard only; then review key flows with a screen reader.

The interviewer goes deeperWhich accessibility failures are difficult to detect from a static DOM scan?

Question #135
My notes & example from experience
136Testing & Quality/SeniorKeep visual regression tests useful
The interview scenario

Every screenshot test changes because of clocks, fonts, avatars, and animation, so reviewers approve all diffs.

How to answer

Control the rendering environment: browser version, viewport, fonts, test data, time-dependent content, and animation. Wait for the specific stable state before capturing. Mask genuinely irrelevant dynamic regions sparingly; do not hide the component whose regression you are trying to detect.

Use a focused baseline set of high-value components and flows. Visual comparisons complement semantic and functional assertions rather than replacing them. A baseline update requires review of why pixels changed; automatically accepting every new image removes the protection.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
await expect(page.getByTestId("product-card"))
  .toHaveScreenshot("product-card.png", { animations: "disabled" });

Common mistake

Increasing pixel tolerances until significant layout regressions no longer fail.

Prove your answer

Introduce a known spacing or clipping error and confirm the selected test catches it.

Question #136
My notes & example from experience
137Testing & Quality/LeadMeasure field performance, not only a Lighthouse score
The interview scenario

A release improves a lab score but worsens performance for users with older phones.

How to answer

Use real-user measurements to understand experienced LCP, INP, and CLS across relevant routes, devices, connection conditions, and release versions. Lab tests provide controlled diagnosis; they do not reproduce the full field distribution. Compare equivalent cohorts and sufficient samples.

Instrument with a maintained measurement library, protect privacy, and avoid collecting sensitive full URLs or form contents. Handle metric updates and lifecycle reporting according to the library's API rather than assuming one simplistic timer per page. Set budgets around user outcomes and investigate regressions with attribution.

import { onLCP, onINP, onCLS } from "web-vitals";
onLCP(reportMetric); onINP(reportMetric); onCLS(reportMetric);
// reportMetric must implement a privacy-reviewed transport and schema.

Comparing unrelated cohorts or averaging away a slow tail of important users.

Question #137
My notes & example from experience
138Testing & Quality/SeniorMake invalid component props unrepresentable
The interview scenario

A dialog accepts loading, error, success, and data props independently, allowing contradictory combinations.

How to answer

Model mutually exclusive states with a discriminated union so each state carries only its valid fields. TypeScript can narrow on the discriminant and make missing cases visible through an exhaustive check. This makes the public component contract easier to understand and test.

Static types do not validate network data or JavaScript callers at runtime. Validate external inputs at the boundary, then convert them into the internal state model. Avoid using assertions merely to force an impossible combination through the compiler.

ILLUSTRATIVE CODE
type Result<T> =
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "error"; message: string }
  | { status: "success"; data: T };
function assertNever(value: never): never {
  throw new Error("Unhandled state");
}
Framework examples are fragments; app helpers and setup may be omitted. Only the Visual Labs execute demonstrations.
Common mistake

Using many unrelated booleans and assuming naming conventions prevent invalid combinations.

Prove your answer

Add a new union member and confirm unhandled render paths fail type checking.

The interviewer goes deeperWhen should loading preserve the previous successful data instead of replacing it?
DocumentationTypeScript: Narrowing ↗MDN: Client-side form validation ↗
Question #138
My notes & example from experience
139Testing & Quality/LeadCapture frontend failures without leaking private data
The interview scenario

A production error dashboard shows minified stack traces with no release context and accidentally logs user input.

How to answer

Collect meaningful failure categories: render failures through appropriate boundaries, uncaught script errors, unhandled promise rejections, and failed resource or API operations through suitable instrumentation. These surfaces are not interchangeable; one global handler does not replace every local recovery path.

Attach a release identifier and privacy-reviewed context, upload source maps securely where appropriate, redact sensitive values, and deduplicate reports. Preserve actionable user recovery. Monitoring should help reproduce the failure without turning URLs, form fields, or authentication tokens into an unintended data store.

Common mistake

Logging every request body or assuming a React error boundary catches every asynchronous event failure.

Prove your answer

Trigger representative failures and inspect the exact telemetry payload for sensitive data.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you connect a client failure to a server trace without exposing credentials?
DocumentationMDN: Window error event ↗React: Error boundaries ↗
Question #139
My notes & example from experience
140Testing & Quality/LeadDesign a frontend CI gate that catches real release risks
The interview scenario

A pipeline runs thousands of unit tests but deploys a build with broken deep links and missing CSS.

How to answer

Layer checks by risk: reproducible dependency installation, type and static checks, focused unit/component tests, a production build, and browser smoke tests against that artifact. Test critical deep links and authenticated flows with controlled data rather than only the development server.

Add targeted visual, accessibility, and bundle checks where their value justifies cost. Keep browser versions and test environments explicit, preserve failure traces, and separate flaky-test remediation from increasing retries. A fast reliable gate plus staged rollout is usually more useful than a slow noisy gate everyone bypasses.

Common mistake

Running end-to-end tests only against a dev server and never testing deployment routing.

Prove your answer

Deliberately break a deep link, asset path, and critical variant to verify the gate fails.

The interviewer goes deeperWhich checks would block a hotfix, and which would run after deployment?

Question #140
My notes & example from experience
141Architecture/LeadDesign an accessible production autocomplete
The interview scenario

Build a search suggestion box for a large catalog. Users type quickly, navigate by keyboard, and experience variable latency.

How to answer

Clarify matching, latency, minimum input, localization, and selection behavior. Keep input updates immediate; debounce appropriate network work, cancel unnecessary requests, and guard against stale completions. Cache by normalized query only when that matches product semantics and privacy requirements.

Implement the combobox interaction contract: names, expanded state, active option, keyboard navigation, selection, and announcements. Handle loading, empty, error, and composition input states. Limit rendering work and measure request volume and input responsiveness. The algorithm and accessible interaction design must be developed together.

Common mistake

Building only the happy-path dropdown and treating arrow keys or stale responses as later polish.

Prove your answer

Test fast typing, out-of-order responses, IME composition, keyboard selection, and empty results.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you keep the active option valid when new results replace the old list?
DocumentationW3C WAI: Combobox pattern ↗MDN: AbortController ↗web.dev: Optimize INP ↗
Question #141
My notes & example from experience
142Architecture/LeadDesign a table with hundreds of thousands of records
The interview scenario

A dashboard needs sorting, filtering, selection, and smooth scrolling over a very large dataset.

How to answer

Separate data volume from rendered DOM volume. Use server-side operations or pagination when transferring all records is inappropriate, and virtualization when the visible window is much smaller than the loaded dataset. Define stable row IDs, selection semantics, cursor behavior, and sorting consistency.

Virtualization introduces trade-offs for variable heights, keyboard focus, browser find, screen readers, printing, and sticky regions. Use overscan deliberately and preserve focus when rows are recycled. A virtualizer reduces rendering work; it does not automatically make a huge download, expensive filter, or unclear selection model efficient.

Common mistake

Virtualizing the DOM but downloading an unnecessarily huge dataset and sorting it on every keystroke.

Prove your answer

Test variable row heights, keyboard navigation, selection across pages, and slow data retrieval.

The interviewer goes deeperDoes select all mean visible rows, loaded rows, or all matching records?
DocumentationTanStack Virtual: Introduction ↗
Question #142
My notes & example from experience
143Architecture/LeadPlace state in the right owner
The interview scenario

A team puts URL filters, server responses, open menus, and form drafts into one global store.

How to answer

Classify state by ownership and lifetime. Shareable navigation state often belongs in the URL; remote server state benefits from a cache with freshness and invalidation semantics; short-lived UI state should stay near its owner. Forms may need a separate draft and validation lifecycle.

Avoid duplicating values that can be derived from a canonical source. A global store can coordinate genuinely shared client state, but it should not become an accidental second database or router. Define how refresh, Back, logout, tab changes, and server mutations affect each category.

Common mistake

Copying query results into a global store without defining which copy is authoritative.

Prove your answer

Test refresh, Back, deep links, logout, and simultaneous views of the same record.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you prevent a form draft from overwriting a newer server revision?

Question #143
My notes & example from experience
144Architecture/LeadDesign a component library as a public product
The interview scenario

Five teams need a shared design system, but every app has different forms and navigation requirements.

How to answer

Define the shared contract around tokens, accessible primitives, stable component APIs, and documented composition patterns. Separate behavior-heavy primitives from product-specific workflows. Establish versioning, ownership, contribution rules, and migration paths before the library becomes a bottleneck.

Provide examples for loading, errors, keyboard behavior, theming, and responsive content, not only ideal screenshots. Test representative consumer integrations and avoid breaking semantic guarantees through unrestricted overrides. Reuse is successful when teams can adopt consistent behavior without forking the implementation for every legitimate variation.

Common mistake

Calling a folder of visual components a design system while leaving semantics and upgrades undefined.

Prove your answer

Build representative flows in two consuming apps and measure how often custom forks are needed.

Question #144
My notes & example from experience
145Architecture/LeadDecide whether microfrontends solve the actual problem
The interview scenario

Two teams want independent releases, and propose splitting one application into many separately deployed frontends.

How to answer

Start with organizational and product boundaries: independent ownership, release cadence, failure isolation, and stable integration contracts. Route-level separation can be simpler than composing many independently versioned runtimes inside one screen. Next.js multi-zones is one documented route-level approach, with hard navigations between zones.

Evaluate duplicated dependencies, navigation continuity, authentication, shared design, observability, deployment routing, and cross-team changes. A modular monolith may solve ownership needs with less operational cost. Choose microfrontends only when their independence benefit exceeds the integration and user-experience costs.

Common mistake

Adopting microfrontends simply because the repository is large.

Prove your answer

Prototype one boundary and measure navigation, bundle duplication, rollback, and cross-team changes.

The interviewer goes deeperWhat shared contract would prevent independently deployed zones from breaking each other?
DocumentationNext.js: Multi-zones ↗
Question #145
My notes & example from experience
146Architecture/LeadMigrate an existing frontend incrementally
The interview scenario

A business-critical legacy application must adopt React or a new rendering approach without a risky rewrite.

How to answer

Find a narrow boundary that can be migrated and verified independently: a route, a widget, or a vertical user journey. Preserve the existing application around that boundary and define explicit data, event, styling, and navigation contracts. React can be added to an existing page rather than replacing everything at once.

Set measurable acceptance criteria and a rollback path. Avoid two systems owning the same DOM subtree or competing copies of state. Migrate shared foundations only when necessary, and use compatibility adapters with planned removal rather than leaving permanent bidirectional coupling.

Common mistake

Rewriting all features before shipping any replacement, or letting two runtimes mutate the same nodes.

Prove your answer

Run old/new behavior comparisons, production smoke tests, and a controlled rollback rehearsal.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you share authentication without sharing all application state?
DocumentationReact: Add to an existing project ↗
Question #146
My notes & example from experience
147Architecture/LeadDesign offline editing and conflict recovery
The interview scenario

Users edit notes offline on two devices. When connectivity returns, one device silently overwrites the other.

How to answer

Separate local drafts, queued operations, and the last acknowledged server revision. Persist enough metadata to retry safely and make synchronization status visible. Use version checks or another explicit conflict strategy rather than assuming last-write-wins is acceptable for every product.

Choose conflict handling by data model: prompt for reconciliation, merge independent fields, or use a specialized collaborative data structure where its complexity is justified. A service worker helps network interception and offline assets but does not decide semantic merges. Protect queued sensitive data and handle logout, expiration, and deleted records.

Common mistake

Equating background synchronization with automatic conflict resolution.

Prove your answer

Test two devices editing one record, deletion while offline, repeated retries, and expired authentication.

The interviewer goes deeperWhen is last-write-wins acceptable, and how would you communicate possible data loss?
DocumentationMDN: Using service workers ↗MDN: Web Storage API ↗MDN: Using Fetch ↗
Question #147
My notes & example from experience
148Architecture/LeadBuild a safe and responsive streaming AI interface
The interview scenario

A chat UI receives partial output, malformed Markdown, cancellation, and occasional repeated stream events.

How to answer

Treat the stream as a sequence of transport chunks, not complete application messages. Decode text incrementally and use explicit framing so a JSON event or multibyte character can span chunks. Model connecting, streaming, completed, canceled, and failed states; keep request identity and cleanup explicit.

Batch visual updates enough to avoid a render per tiny token, preserve deliberate scrolling behavior, and make accessible announcements less noisy than token-by-token narration. Treat model output as untrusted content, and keep privileged tool execution and authorization outside the model's textual instructions. Cancellation must not imply undoing already committed server work.

Common mistake

Calling JSON.parse on every raw network chunk or inserting model output directly as HTML.

Prove your answer

Test split UTF-8 characters, split events, malicious links, aborts, reconnection, and slow rendering.

The interviewer goes deeperHow would you preserve a user's scroll position while new tokens arrive?
DocumentationMDN: Readable streams ↗OWASP: XSS prevention ↗MDN: AbortController ↗
Question #148
My notes & example from experience
149Architecture/LeadPlan an optimistic update with honest recovery
The interview scenario

A user likes a post instantly, but the request fails or the same action is performed from another tab.

How to answer

Identify whether the operation is safely reversible and whether immediate feedback improves the experience. Keep a confirmed baseline and pending operation identity, then reconcile the server's authoritative result. Prevent a late failure from undoing a newer successful action.

Choose clear pending and failure feedback, retry rules, and duplicate-submission handling. Counts, permissions, and concurrent edits may require server recomputation rather than local arithmetic. An optimistic interface is a prediction with a recovery contract, not permission to ignore validation or to pretend a failed mutation succeeded.

Common mistake

Rolling back to an old snapshot that discards unrelated newer updates.

Prove your answer

Test rapid toggles, out-of-order completions, duplicate requests, and changes from another tab.

The interviewer goes deeperWhich operations should not be optimistic in your product, and why?
DocumentationReact: useOptimistic ↗MDN: Using Fetch ↗
Question #149
My notes & example from experience
150Architecture/LeadLead a production frontend incident investigation
The interview scenario

After a rollout, checkout conversion drops and some users report a frozen Pay button. How do you respond?

How to answer

Clarify impact and establish a timeline, affected routes, browsers, cohorts, and release identifiers. Stabilize first when risk warrants it: roll back, disable the feature, or route users to a safe path. Preserve enough evidence to investigate without collecting sensitive payment or personal data.

Compare failing and healthy cohorts using errors, request outcomes, performance traces, and session-safe reproduction. Form testable hypotheses across UI state, JavaScript exceptions, network/authentication, third parties, and deployment assets. Verify the fix with a targeted regression test and staged rollout; then address monitoring and process gaps rather than assigning blame.

Common mistake

Blaming React rendering immediately without checking whether the click reaches the server.

Prove your answer

Reproduce the failure, make the regression test fail before the fix, and monitor the same affected cohort afterward.

Who runs first?

Predict the output before pressing Run. The timer has a zero delay, but that does not make it synchronous.

log('A'); setTimeout(() => log('B'), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => log('C'));
queueMicrotask(() => log('D')); log('E');
Your prediction: ____
SynchronousMicrotaskTimer task

Microtasks run before this timer task. Paint is not guaranteed after every task.Question 001 ↗

02 / React · state-queue simulation

One snapshot. Three updates.

Compare replacing a value with applying an updater function. This models one event's queued updates, not React scheduling.

Select an update strategy
Initial: 0
Committed result
0

Replacement expressions use the same render snapshot; updater functions receive the previous queued result.Question 025 ↗

03 / JavaScript · simulated requests

Newest intent vs. last response

Request A starts first but is slow. B starts later and finishes first. Compare an unguarded UI with a request-identity guard.

A · 900ms
B · 250ms
No identity checkWaiting
Latest intent winsWaiting
No network traffic is sent.

Cancellation saves work where supported; identity checks protect the UI from stale completion.Question 007 ↗

04 / JavaScript · real timers

Debounce or throttle?

Each bar is one callback. Debounce waits for 300ms of quiet. This leading-only throttle accepts at most one event every 300ms.

Raw events
0
Debounced
0
Throttled
0

Burst spacing is 100ms; actual timer execution can be delayed by the browser. Latest 24 callback marks are shown.Question 009 ↗

05 / CSS · real layout

Where did the extra width go?

Declared width: 180px. Border: 4px on each side. Change padding and switch the sizing model to see the measured border box.

Content

The outer margin is not included in either border-box calculation.Question 101 ↗

06 / CSS + Tailwind · real container query

The card knows its own space

Keep the browser window still. Resize only this parent. At 320px of queryable content width, its child switches from stacked to horizontal.

Reusable card

One component. Different parents.

.parent { container-type: inline-size; }
@container (min-width: 320px) { /* child layout */ }

Tailwind's @container variants express this local-sizing model. On narrow screens the parent is capped to its available space.Question 123 ↗

07 / CSS · real stacking contexts

A million is still not enough

The green tooltip has z-index: 999999. It still loses to panel B because its parent A is in a lower stacking context.

Parent A · z-index: 1
Tooltip
z-index: 999999
Panel B
z-index: 2

The child cannot escape the order of its parent's stacking context.Question 106 ↗

08 / Next.js · cache-policy simulation

Refresh does not mean invalidate

Change the origin, then read. A fresh cache can still return old data. Compare stale-while-revalidate with immediate expiry. No Next.js runtime is loaded.

Originv1
Server cachev1
UIv1
Cache is fresh
Origin and cache both start at v1.

Teaching analogy: revalidateTag(tag, 'max') uses SWR; updateTag expires immediately in Server Actions. router.refresh alone does not invalidate the server data cache.Question 062 ↗

A suggested path, not a fixed schedule

Practice for depth

For senior interviews, explain the mechanism and show how you would verify it in a real application.

Use each question twice. First answer it aloud without opening the explanation. Then compare your answer, run the relevant lab, and add an example from your own work. Mark confident only when you can explain the trade-off and the failure mode.
Session 01

JavaScript under pressure

Event loops, closures, asynchronous work, cancellation, and data transformations.

Session 02

React behavior

State snapshots, Effects, rendering, concurrency, and current APIs.

Session 03

Next.js architecture

Rendering boundaries, caching, navigation, server mutations, and deployment.

Session 04

The browser is the platform

Loading, performance, security, accessibility, and resilience.

Session 05

CSS and component styling

Intrinsic sizing, Grid, stacking, container queries, and Tailwind v4.

Session 06

Quality and trade-offs

Behavior tests, field performance, frontend system design, and safe rollouts.

Session 07 / Mock interview

Turn knowledge into an explanation

Start a mixed 10-question session. For each answer, cover: mechanism, concrete example, trade-off, failure mode, and verification. Use the follow-up to challenge your first solution. Your rating is self-assessment, not automated grading.

Keep the experience-level distinction clear

Foundation / Mid: Explain the browser or language rule and demonstrate a correct implementation. Senior: Discuss edge cases, accessibility, performance, and testing. Lead: Add ownership, operational risks, migration, and rollout decisions. These labels are editorial learning guides, not a hiring-company scoring standard.

Scope and methodology. These are original interview-style scenarios grounded in official framework, platform, accessibility, and security documentation. They are not claimed to be leaked company questions, measured interview-frequency rankings, or a guarantee of what a particular employer asks. Browser-dependent and opt-in features are labeled. Diagrams are explanatory simplifications, and framework code snippets are illustrative fragments rather than complete applications.
